description: Analytical compare of equal_count_breath ingested evidence. Not a kernel. Not canon. Canon: docs/practices/PRACTICE_TECHNIQUE_NORMALIZATION_V1.md

mechanism.question: Do the records describe the same kind of action: regulated cyclic breathing with timed phases?
mechanism.shared: All three write a repeating timed breath cycle with an equal count on the phases they include.
mechanism.divergence: They do not agree how many timed phases the cycle contains.

identity_bearing_steps.question: Which phases are required for the method to be this method?
identity_bearing_steps.landscape_prior: Landscape mechanism_shape treated four equal phases including pauses as family identity.
identity_bearing_steps.bhf_sfh: Both write inhale, pause, exhale, pause.
identity_bearing_steps.newcastle: Writes inhale, pause, exhale, then repeat. Does not write a pause after the exhale.
identity_bearing_steps.not_used: Two-against-one count of loci does not decide which phase set is identity-bearing.

bounds.question: Is equal count / count-of-four part of the method, or an expression parameter?
bounds.observed: All three illustrate a count of four. None argues that four is the method rather than a convenient default. Session length and cycle count differ by locus.

variants_vs_conflicts.question: Does absence of the post-exhale hold change the technique, or remain an allowed variation?
variants_vs_conflicts.locus_offered_options: Posture, tracing a square, hands on the belly, and how long to continue are options the four-phase pages themselves offer.
variants_vs_conflicts.phase_mismatch: Ingest recorded the missing post-exhale hold as a conflicting description, not as a variant. This pass does not reverse that.

why_not_normalize_one: Declaring the post-exhale hold optional would add a claim ingest did not make.
Landscape already treated pauses as identity-bearing; this pass cannot silently demote that.
Shared names (box / square) are not a kernel.
why_not_split_family: No selected locus says the three-phase page is a different method from the four-phase pages.
The same labels appear on structurally different sequences. That may be a naming collision, not two families.
Splitting now would freeze landscape before the identity question is researched.
research_question: Is post-exhale hold identity-bearing for the box/square/equal-count breathing family, or do sources use one name for structurally different methods?
